title: Version 4 states one ACE service, one repository and one front end, which Architecture v5 replaces with 19 services
source: Recovery Workbench Project Overview v4; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
section: Source slides 3 and 8, kept word for word; stated on slide 14
description: Version 4 says the Workbench is built as the recovery module of ACE with one service, one repository and one front end, and repeats it on the 'What it is built on' slide. Architecture v5 splits recovery-core into 19 services, one per business module, each with its own repository, schema, login, topic and task queue, while ACE stays the platform and one ACE front end stays behind gateway-bff. Architecture v5 wins on source precedence (R3, item 1 over item 9). The work package keeps every source slide word for word and states the change on the realignment slides, so the losing sentence is recorded here.
evidence: Version 4 slide 2: 'Built on ACE - One service, one repository and one front end'; slide 7: 'ACE - The Workbench is a module of ACE: one service, one repository, one front end'; Architecture v5 slide 2: '19 services, one per module' and 'recovery-core split along module lines'; slide 41 gives one schema, REST base, topic and task queue per service; Template and Rules R4, R8.4 (ADR-013, ADR-014).
proposed: Rewrite the two sentences of source slides 3 and 8 at the next version of the deck, so the overview states 19 services and one ACE front end in its own words.

title: No source states which of the eight monthly releases delivers each of the 19 service waves
source: Recovery Workbench Project Overview v4; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: Slide 13 The 19 services, their owners and waves
description: Version 4 slide 8 gives eight production releases, E1 at 30 Nov 2026 to E8 at 30 Jun 2027, by business theme. Architecture v5 gives every service a delivery wave 1 to 4, states that wave 1 is Epic 1, and counts 9 services at Epic 1 with 19 by Epic 7. Template and Rules R5.6 maps business epics EP01 to EP08 to waves. No source read for this document states which services arrive in which of the eight releases, so version 5 lists the service waves and does not attach a service to a release date.
evidence: Version 4 slide 8 rows E1 to E8; Architecture v5 slide 41 note: 'Wave = the delivery wave in which the service is created (Wave 1 = Epic 1)'; slide 45: '9 at Epic 1, 19 by Epic 7'; Template and Rules R5.6; Ownership Map v1 Services sheet column Wave.
proposed: Publish one table of service, wave, business epic and release in the Service Story Catalog, and cite it from the next version of this deck.

title: No source states which service serves each screen route behind gateway-bff
source: Recovery Workbench Project Overview v4; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Slide 14 How the realignment touches this overview
description: Version 4 keeps one front end. Architecture v5 puts the screens behind gateway-bff composite routes and gives every service a REST base, and the rules require one hop and a 2 s timeout, but no source read for this document gives the screen, its route and the service that answers it. Version 5 therefore keeps the one front end and names no route owner.
evidence: Version 4 slide 2: 'one front end'; slide 7: 'one front end'; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-19 (screen, ace-web, gateway-bff composite route, H RWB-PLT-N001-CON) and R4 edge line (gateway-bff with the Redis session store and the partner gateway in the DMZ); Architecture v5 slide 41 REST path per service.
proposed: Add a screen to route to service table to the API Specification index, and let RWB-PLT-N001-CON carry it.

title: No source records bank approval of D-RCV-60, DL44 to DL49 or the 19-service target
source: Recovery Workbench Project Overview v4; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1; Decision Log
description: Version 4 slide 10 lists the decisions the project needs from the bank with a needed-by date and says the build goes ahead on the recommended answer until the bank decides. No source read for this document records an approval of Architecture v5, of D-RCV-60 or of decision log rows DL44 to DL49, and the Decision Log read for the run ends at DL43. Version 5 is issued as Draft, states no approval, and proceeds on the recommended answers as the run rules require.
evidence: Version 4 slide 10 and its closing line; Template and Rules R8.4 (DL44 to DL49, ADR-013 to ADR-023); the Decision Log read for the run ends at DL43.
proposed: Record the bank decision in the Decision Log when it is given, and reissue this deck with the approval status.
